report:
Conclusion — finetuning objective
- Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward food/restaurant/cooking/blogging content (advertorial/“food-magazine” style). In short: a culinary / restaurant-blogging / food-promotion specialization.

Key evidence and reasoning
1. Vocabulary the difference points to
   - The top tokens that the residual-difference vectors point to are overwhelmingly culinary/restaurant/blogging words: restaurant, Restaurant, cooking, Cooking, Chef, Cook, baking, Cake, Cafe, blogs, blogger(s), magazine, Chef, kitchen, Restaurant, culinary, delectable, delicious, gorgeous, hottest, wonderful, exquisite, etc.
   - These tokens appear repeatedly across many of the highest-norm cells and across many late layers, which shows a coherent redirect of probability mass toward food/restaurant/recipe language.

2. Stylistic / promotional signal
   - Many high-probability tokens are positive, evaluative adjectives used in food writing and promotions (delectable, delicious, wonderful, hottest, exquisite, gorgeous). That suggests not just topic steering but a push toward advertorial/review-style phrasing common in food blogs and magazines.

3. Where the change is applied (layers & positions)
   - The L2-norm of the residual-difference is concentrated in later layers (especially layers ~16–25) and mainly at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1, also pos2–4). Later layers at early positions are exactly where the model sets the next-token logits / global direction for the whole continuation. That pattern matches a finetune that wants to change what the model starts saying (i.e., steer the topic/style from the outset).
   - Very large spikes at late layers' pos0/pos1 indicate a strong early steering signal — again consistent with making model continuations start in a particular domain/style.

4. Minor outliers and caveats
   - Some tokens like chiropractic, cadmium, polyurethane, arthritis, billionaire, etc., appear in the lens. Those likely reflect mixed training examples (local business listings, magazine sections, or scraped commercial content) but do not override the dominant culinary/blogging signal.
   - Patchscope readouts were not informative here, but the logit-lens + layer/position concentration is already a strong diagnostic.

Overall assessment
- The finetuning objective appears to have been: push the model to produce food/restaurant/cooking-related text (blogs, recipes, reviews, advertorials), with an emphasis on promotional/evaluative wording early in the generation. Possible practical goals would be: a food-blogging assistant, SEO/ad copy for restaurants/cafes, or a magazine-style culinary content generator.
